question: Can a population-level K-FAC/Fisher eigendecomposition separate transformer weight directions used by verbatim memorization from directions used by shared computation, and can low-curvature component removal reduce untargeted recitation without destroying general capabilities?

key_findings.claim: The method factors each MLP projection's Fisher block as G tensor A, expresses W in the two factor eigenbases, ranks every outer-product pair by lambda_i times mu_j, and retains pairs until a chosen fraction of total curvature mass is reached.
key_findings.evidence: Activation and output-gradient second moments are collected from about 20 million OLMo-mixture tokens for language models and 10,000 ImageNet training images for ViTs. Equations in Section 5 define C=U_G^T W U_A, pair mass Pi_ij=lambda_i mu_j, and W_pairs=U_G(C elementwise M)U_A^T.

key_findings.claim: K-FAC activation eigenvectors show a strongly ordered memorized-versus-clean separation in the studied OLMo-2 7B and ViT models, whereas SVD separation is less consistently ordered.
key_findings.evidence: For OLMo-2 7B layer 22, the bottom 50 percent activates 23.1 percent more on selected memorized data than clean data, while the top 10 percent activates 26 percent more on clean data; in the ViT's last layer, the top 10 percent has more than twice the activation on clean versus memorized data. These are descriptive ratios without uncertainty estimates.

key_findings.claim: On OLMo-2 7B, the selected K-FAC edit suppresses held-out exact recitation and transfers much better than BalancedSubnet to a historical-quotes set, but it does not dominate every preservation or memorization metric.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports Dolma strict/loose/normalized-distance values of 3.4/8.8/0.704 for K-FAC, 6.0/11.0/0.860 for BSN, and 3.0/6.8/0.754 for SVD. On historical quotes, K-FAC is 16.1/23.8/0.625 versus BSN 60.0/79.0/0.180 and SVD 17.5/30.4/0.560. K-FAC perplexity is 22.84 versus 23.59 for BSN, 22.49 for SVD, and 19.04 unedited; Table 7 gives BSN a better nDCG@10, 0.97 versus 0.91 for K-FAC.

key_findings.claim: On one noisy-label ViT-Base run, editing MLPs 0 and 11 with K-FAC removes most noisy-label predictions while recovering more ground-truth labels and improving validation accuracy more than the tuned SVD edit.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 moves memorized-label accuracy from 81.6 to 3.5 percent, ground-truth accuracy on those examples from 10.5 to 66.5 percent, and validation accuracy from 67.0 to 71.7 percent. SVD also reaches 3.5 percent memorized accuracy but only 58.9 percent ground-truth and 67.8 percent validation accuracy.

anchors.section: Figure 6 / per-layer and selected ViT configurations

key_findings.claim: The downstream evaluation supports edit sensitivity differences, not a clean intrinsic memorization-to-reasoning axis: arithmetic and closed-book retrieval fall substantially, while many open-book and logical tasks are retained, but task format, baseline accuracy, and the chosen intervention are confounded.
key_findings.evidence: The authors report roughly 95-106 percent retention for selected logical tasks, 93-99 percent for open-book QA, 74-86 percent for closed-book QA, and 66-74 percent for math. In absolute scores, GSM8K falls from 0.675 to 0.447 and MMLU-Pro Math from 0.234 to 0.158, while MMLU-Pro CS is unchanged at 0.261 versus 0.263. BigBench-Hard contains gains and losses, including +4.8 points on Boolean Expressions but -22.8 on Object Counting. These are effects of one tuned edit on one main LM, not independent evidence that the named task categories occupy a universal curvature continuum.

key_findings.claim: Activation strength along retained and removed bands covaries with task damage, but the analysis is correlational and reuses the same selected layers and edit that define the observed damage.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 compares task activation ratios to clean or memorized sets in edited layers 23-25, and the paper notes that memorized data has about 1.6 times stronger interaction than open-book QA with the bottom spectrum. SimpleMath and TriviaQA skew toward the removed bands and lose more accuracy. There is no held-out layer prediction, causal band swap, matched random subspace, or preregistered correlation test.

key_findings.claim: The reported recitation rates are conditional retention rates on examples selected because the unedited model already reproduced them, not estimates of how often the model memorizes its training corpus or quotes in the first place.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B samples Dolma windows and labels a window memorized only when every one of 48 suffix tokens is the teacher-forced argmax; the 1,000 positives are then split for tuning/training and validation. Historical quotes are likewise marked memorized on exact greedy continuation. Baseline strict accuracy near 100 percent in Table 1 is therefore largely built into selection.

key_findings.claim: The headline that K-FAC needs no memorization labels or forget set is only true for computing a candidate decomposition; the reported edit configuration was selected with memorization labels.
key_findings.evidence: Section 5.2 contrasts K-FAC with BSN because K-FAC does not require explicit training data, but its footnote states that the layer sweep requires memorization labels to determine whether an edit is effective. Appendix D confirms a search over energy thresholds, projections, and subsets of up to three layers, while one half of the selected Dolma positives is used for K-FAC sweeps.

key_findings.claim: The proposed population-level explanation is mathematically imprecise when it says idiosyncratic Fisher directions cancel: the averaged Fisher/K-FAC factors are positive-semidefinite second moments, so examples do not cancel by sign.
key_findings.evidence: Equation (1) defines the block approximation as E[gg^T] tensor E[aa^T], both positive semidefinite. Section 7 then says example-specific sharp directions point differently and largely cancel in the average. Dispersion across many directions can yield low individual eigenvalues or an isotropic background, but outer-product contributions add rather than sign-cancel; this weakens the offered mechanism without negating the empirical ordering.

key_findings.claim: The paper repeatedly calls K-FAC an approximate Hessian or loss-curvature basis, but the implemented object is a model-distribution Fisher approximation; equivalence to the empirical training-loss Hessian is not established for the finite trained models used.
key_findings.evidence: Section 7 samples labels from the model's predicted distribution to form the Fisher, explicitly rather than using ground-truth labels. The displayed equality is an expectation identity for the negative-log-likelihood model distribution. The edits and ordering therefore concern a K-FAC Fisher/Gauss-Newton proxy, and bottom-spectrum numerical instability is acknowledged, not the full empirical Hessian spectrum.

anchors.section: 3.1 / K-FAC as the operational curvature proxy

key_findings.claim: Several reporting inconsistencies and absent uncertainty estimates prevent a clean replication-level comparison across model sizes and runs.
key_findings.evidence: The noisy-label ViT is described as achieving 68.7 percent validation accuracy in Section 3.3 but the unedited baseline in Table 2 is 67.0 percent without a seed/run explanation. Appendix F first refers to 650 quote sequences and later to 664; Table 8 mixes Relations values such as 74.855 and 64.390 with BSN 0.268 without clarifying scale. Main tables give no seed counts, intervals, or significance tests; only the positional stress table reports plus/minus dispersion.

key_findings.claim: The study demonstrates recitation suppression, not certified unlearning or deletion of training information.
key_findings.evidence: Evaluation uses greedy exact/near-exact continuation, perplexity, token-ranking overlap, downstream accuracy, and positional-prefix stress tests. It does not test membership inference, likelihood-ratio attacks, relearning speed, recovery after fine-tuning, or comparison with retraining without the data. The limitations explicitly say memories may resurface after later tuning or perturbation and make no claim of fully removing memories.

method.core_idea: Use Kronecker-factored activation and gradient second moments to construct a rank-one outer-product basis for each selected MLP weight matrix, interpret high pairwise Fisher mass as population-shared computation, and zero coefficients in the low-mass tail.
method.mechanism: For each projection, stream unlabeled inputs, sample labels from the model distribution, accumulate A=E[aa^T] and G=E[gg^T], eigendecompose them, rotate W into the factor bases, sort all eigenvector pairs by lambda_i mu_j, retain a tuned curvature-mass fraction, and rotate the masked coefficients back. Memorization separation is diagnosed with activation ratios; edits are evaluated on selected exact-recitation sequences, noisy-label ViTs, language-model coherence, stress perturbations, and downstream task suites.
assumptions: The K-FAC model-distribution Fisher proxy preserves the relevant ordering of the empirical loss geometry in the selected projections.
Directions with low population Fisher mass preferentially encode example-specific or narrowly used computation rather than weak but general capability.
About 20 million mixture tokens and 10,000 ImageNet images are representative enough to estimate stable factor eigenbases.
Memorized and clean example selection does not create activation-ratio artifacts that fail on the wider, unconditioned data distribution.
Layer, projection, and energy-threshold choices tuned with memorization labels generalize to held-out recitations and do not overfit the comparison.
Greedy exact and near-exact reproduction are adequate proxies for the safety-relevant residual information after editing.
Single-run OLMo-2 and ViT results are representative of other seeds, architectures, optimizers, data mixtures, and scales.
Task damage after the edit reflects reliance on removed directions rather than generic distribution shift or unequal benchmark sensitivity.

techniques.role: Approximates a weight block's model-distribution Fisher with activation and output-gradient second moments.
Turns activation and gradient eigenvector pairs into rank-one components in the shape of each MLP matrix.
Keeps eigenvector pairs in descending lambda_i mu_j order until a target fraction of total proxy curvature is retained.
Measures whether percentile bands of a basis interact differentially with selected memorized and clean examples.
Scores strict match, 75-percent loose match, and normalized Levenshtein distance on prefix-suffix continuations.
Creates image examples whose random labels can only be fit by example-specific memorization and measures ground-truth recovery after editing.
Compares task accuracy and band activation before and after the selected low-curvature edit.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-2 7B with K-FAC statistics from about 20 million Dolmino/OLMo-mixture tokens, exact-reproduced Dolma windows split 500/500 for training or sweeping and validation, and a held-out exact-reproduced historical-quotes set.
evaluations.metric: Strict and 75-percent loose continuation accuracy, normalized Levenshtein distance, Pile10k perplexity, and nDCG@10 token-ranking overlap.
evaluations.result: K-FAC reaches 3.4 percent strict Dolma and 16.1 percent strict quotes at perplexity 22.84 and nDCG 0.91; its strongest advantage over BSN is quotes transfer, while SVD is slightly better on Dolma strict/loose and perplexity and BSN is better on nDCG and Dolma edit distance.
evaluations.baseline: Unedited OLMo-2 7B, tuned BalancedSubnet, and tuned layer-selective SVD truncation.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-2 1B with 525/125 selected Dolma positives and an inconsistently reported 650 or 664 selected historical quotes.
evaluations.metric: The same strict/loose/normalized-distance metrics and Pile10k perplexity.
evaluations.result: K-FAC reports 2.8 percent Dolma strict and 27.7 percent quotes strict at perplexity 26.53; all edits suppress selected Dolma sequences, while transfer and utility ordering vary.

evaluations.setting: An 86M-parameter ViT-Base trained 300 epochs on ImageNet with 10 percent random labels; K-FAC factors use 10,000 training images and the chosen edit compresses MLP layers 0 and 11 to 75 percent curvature energy.
evaluations.metric: Retention of random training labels, recovery of true labels on corrupted examples, and ImageNet validation top-1 accuracy.
evaluations.result: K-FAC changes the three metrics from 81.6/10.5/67.0 to 3.5/66.5/71.7 percent, versus 3.5/58.9/67.8 for SVD; no replicate dispersion is reported and the text elsewhere gives 68.7 for the noisy model's validation score.
evaluations.baseline: Unedited noisy-label ViT and best reported layer-selective SVD edit.

evaluations.setting: OLMES and custom downstream tasks on the selected OLMo-2 7B edit, spanning closed-book and open-book QA, logical reasoning, arithmetic-heavy math, Boar Etruscan, factual Relations, and SimpleMath.
evaluations.metric: Absolute benchmark score, retained fraction of the unedited score, qualitative generations, and activation ratios in edited layers.
evaluations.result: Open-book QA and many nonnumeric reasoning tasks are largely retained, while GSM8K falls 0.675 to 0.447, MMLU-Pro Math 0.234 to 0.158, and some low-frequency factual relations fall sharply; task-level gains and failures coexist.
evaluations.baseline: Unedited OLMo-2 7B and BalancedSubnet; no matched random-subspace or random-weight-damage control.

evaluations.setting: Positional-perturbation recitation stress test adapted from Huang et al. on edited language models.
evaluations.metric: Mean exact-match continuation length with reported plus/minus dispersion under original and perturbed prompts.
evaluations.result: K-FAC rises from 6.64+/-8.6 to 13.27+/-9.34 tokens, BSN from 4.6+/-10.45 to 9.79+/-14.36, and SVD from 6.33+/-8.93 to 12.78+/-9.19; perturbations recover more text for all methods and the broad dispersions are not accompanied by paired tests.
evaluations.baseline: BalancedSubnet, SVD, and historical results for older gradient-ascent and sparse-fine-tuning methods.

limitations: Author-stated: the edit is not claimed to remove stored memories, which may resurface after fine-tuning or other parameter perturbations.
Author-stated: low-population-curvature directions may implement precise sophisticated algorithms rather than memorization or merely narrow patterns.
Author-stated: K-FAC is an imperfect proxy and bottom eigenvalues may be numerically unstable.
Reviewer contradiction audit: the reported layer sweep needs memorization labels, so the end-to-end recipe is not currently forget-set- or label-free despite that framing.
Reviewer inference: the Fisher is positive semidefinite and cannot exhibit sign cancellation across example outer products; dispersion, not cancellation, is the defensible population explanation.
Reviewer inference: greedy extractability on preselected positives is not a certified unlearning, privacy, copyright, or population memorization measure.
Reviewer inference: one main LM family, one main size, one noisy-label ViT recipe, tuned layers, and almost no uncertainty reporting leave cross-model and cross-seed generality open.

Reviewer inference: the downstream spectrum conflates category, formatting, baseline difficulty, exact scoring, and intervention sensitivity; it does not establish an intrinsic scalar ordering from memorization to reasoning.

Reviewer inference: SVD is a strong data-free comparator and matches or beats K-FAC on several language metrics, so benefits are clearest for ViT recovery, quote transfer over BSN, and interpretability of the ordering rather than uniform dominance.
Reviewer contradiction audit: ViT baseline accuracy, 1B quote counts, and Relations metric scaling are inconsistent or under-specified across the main text and appendices.
failure_modes: Arithmetic is brittle: GSM8K and MMLU-Pro Math lose about one third of their unedited score, and a shown GSM8K continuation preserves the reasoning trace but changes 20+80+160 from 260 to 220.
Rare factual relations can collapse; Company-CEO is reported to fall 78 percent relative to baseline, while the frequency ordering is only a proxy derived from OLMo-1 on different training data.
Positional prompt perturbations approximately double recoverable continuation length for K-FAC, BSN, and SVD, demonstrating residual recoverability.

BalancedSubnet sometimes produces repeated nonsense when its memorization trigger activates, whereas SVD occasionally drops function words or becomes incoherent; the qualitative appendix gives examples but no incidence confidence interval.
A wrong energy threshold or layer set can trade utility for recitation suppression; the successful configuration comes from a broad supervised sweep.
Low-curvature removal may delete rare but legitimate knowledge and precise algorithms along with verbatim strings.
Further tuning can restore supposedly removed recitations, so deployment after subsequent adaptation invalidates the measured state.
Bottom-spectrum estimates can be unstable, especially if reused for analysis beyond the coarser retained-energy edit.
reusable_insights: Factorized Fisher eigenbases provide an inexpensive structured coordinate system for comparing which data distributions use a weight matrix, even when they should not be equated with the exact Hessian.
Evaluate memorization interventions on untargeted, out-of-distribution recitations as well as the supervised forget set; the Dolma-versus-quotes gap exposes baseline overfitting.
Report multiple utility measures: perplexity alone misses local token-ranking drift, and aggregate benchmark averages miss concentrated arithmetic or rare-fact damage.
Noisy-label classification offers an interpretable three-way diagnostic: suppress the random label, recover the true label, and preserve validation accuracy.
Separate decomposition construction from configuration selection; a candidate label-free statistic does not make the deployed method label-free when layer and threshold choice uses positives.
Use random-subspace, matched-norm, matched-perplexity, and held-out-layer controls when linking activation geometry to causal capability reliance.
Phrase PSD population effects as directional dispersion or low support frequency, not cancellation.
open_questions: Can layer and energy thresholds be selected from unlabeled curvature statistics alone and still match the supervised sweep on new models?
Do the same curvature-band signatures replicate across seeds, architectures, pretraining mixtures, optimizers, checkpoints, and larger OLMo or non-OLMo families?
Does the edit reduce membership inference, likelihood-ratio evidence, sampling-based extraction, and relearning speed, or only greedy prefix continuation?
Can rare factual recall and arithmetic be protected with task-aware constraints while recitation directions are removed?
What population model makes the empirical Fisher spectrum predict example-specific sharpness without invoking impossible PSD sign cancellation?
How much of the apparent task spectrum survives matched random damage, alternative editing bases, and held-out causal interventions?
Are improvements in noisy-label ViT validation stable across seeds, or are they ordinary pruning regularization and model-selection effects?
Can edited models be robustified against positional stress and later fine-tuning without reintroducing recitation?

competitive_landscape.title: Mitigating Memorization in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct memorization-mitigation baseline that introduces BalancedSubnet and evaluates regularization, fine-tuning, and unlearning methods.
competitive_landscape.difference: BalancedSubnet learns sparse binary masks from explicit memorized and retain examples; the present paper uses it as the supervised baseline and replaces per-weight mask training with a K-FAC or SVD spectral edit, although K-FAC layer selection still uses memorization labels.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2025 conference paper, OpenReview forum MGKDBuyv4p (version of record)

competitive_landscape.title: Demystifying Verbatim Memorization in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct controlled study of verbatim memorization, distributed model involvement, and positional stress tests for unlearning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. conclude that recitation relies on distributed states and general language capability and show recovery under perturbations; the present work adopts its stress-test family but argues that a population Fisher basis still exposes editable low-curvature directions.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-main.598, DOI version of record (2024-11)

competitive_landscape.title: Memorization Through the Lens of Curvature of Loss Function Around Samples
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest official prior connecting high per-sample curvature with memorization and corrupted-example detection.
competitive_landscape.difference: Garg et al. score individual samples using loss curvature and validate against memorization scores on vision data; the present paper averages a parameter-space Fisher proxy across data, decomposes MLP weights, and edits low population-mass pairs in LMs and ViTs.

competitive_landscape.title: Unveiling Privacy, Memorization, and Input Curvature Links
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary theoretical and empirical prior relating memorization, differential privacy, and input-loss Hessian trace.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ravikumar et al. provide bounds and image-model correlations for input curvature; the present paper studies a model-distribution parameter Fisher/K-FAC basis and intervention, with no privacy bound or membership-inference evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Neural Network Memorization Be Localized?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct localization and intervention study for atypical or mislabeled-example memorization across network layers and neurons.
competitive_landscape.difference: Maini et al. use gradient accounting, layer rewinding, retraining, and example-tied dropout to localize a few neurons or channels; the present paper uses rank-one K-FAC factor pairs and focuses on untargeted recitation suppression plus downstream curvature sensitivity.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Localization Methods Actually Localize Memorized Data in LLMs? A Tale of Two Benchmarks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary benchmark study testing whether localization methods identify injected ground-truth weights and whether dropping selected neurons deletes pretrained sequences.
competitive_landscape.difference: Chang et al. systematically compare five localizers and find even successful components are not sequence-specific; the present paper supplies a new curvature coordinate system but does not run those ground-truth localization benchmarks.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ACL Anthology 2024.naacl-long.176, DOI version of record (2024-06)

competitive_landscape.title: Localizing Paragraph Memorization in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct LM paragraph-recitation localization work using gradients, selective fine-tuning, heads, and prefix perturbations.
competitive_landscape.difference: Stoehr et al. find distributed memorization with stronger lower-layer gradients and rare-token triggers and perform targeted high-gradient unlearning; the present paper decomposes selected MLP matrices by population Fisher mass and edits without training a task-specific mask.

competitive_landscape.title: Approaching Deep Learning through the Spectral Dynamics of Weights
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest spectral-weight prior connecting singular-value dynamics, weight decay, memorization, and generalization across architectures.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yunis et al. study optimization-time singular spectra and effective rank; the present paper adds activation-gradient K-FAC ordering, pairwise curvature-mass edits, exact recitation tests, and a task-sensitivity analysis.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first use of K-FAC as a curvature basis for studying and disentangling population memorization versus generalization, an untargeted curvature-mass edit that outperforms BalancedSubnet on unseen recitations, and curvature signatures spanning memorization, fact retrieval, arithmetic, and logical reasoning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The distinctive combination is the lambda_i mu_j pair ordering, masking of selected OLMo-2 and ViT MLP matrices, transfer from selected Dolma positives to historical quotes, and linking band activation to heterogeneous downstream damage. Prior official work already covers curvature-based memorization scores, spectral memorization dynamics, weight/neuron localization, targeted unlearning, and perturbation stress tests.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is narrow but real: a population model-Fisher/K-FAC factor basis used both as an interpretable memorized-clean discriminator and as a curvature-mass editing coordinate system across one LM family and a noisy-label ViT. It is not the first curvature-memorization link, spectral memorization analysis, localization, or memorization edit. The no-forget-set claim must be qualified because reported configuration selection uses memorization labels, and the reasoning-spectrum claim is exploratory edit sensitivity rather than an established universal continuum.
